message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a tenant in Texas. (This is general information and not legal advice; for specific situations you may want to consult an attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.) | Area | What the law says | Practical Tips | |------|-------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge a security deposit, but it cannot exceed **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit or **three months’ rent** for a furnished unit.
• The deposit must be held in a **separate, interest‑bearing account** (unless the landlord is a Texas bank).
• Within **30 days** after you move out, the landlord must return the deposit (or provide a written itemized list of deductions) | • Get a written receipt for the deposit.
• Take photos or videos of the unit before moving in and after moving out. | | **Habitability** | • Landlords must keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition**. This includes functioning plumbing, heating, electrical, and structural integrity.
• The landlord must repair any major defects within a reasonable time after notice. | • Report problems in writing (email or text) and keep copies.
• If repairs are not made, you may withhold rent or make the repairs yourself and deduct the cost (but only after giving the landlord a written notice and a reasonable deadline). | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are **reasonable** (usually not more than 5% of the monthly rent). | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if you’re having trouble. | | **Entry Rights** | • Landlords must give **at least 24 hours’ written notice** before entering, except in emergencies.
• Entry is allowed for inspections, repairs, or to show the unit to prospective tenants or buyers. | • Keep a log of all entries. | | **Privacy** | • Landlords cannot harass or threaten you.
• They cannot use your personal information for discriminatory purposes. | • Document any harassment or threats. | | **Discrimination** | • Under the **Fair Housing Act** and Texas law, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • If you suspect discrimination, file a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party can terminate a lease with proper notice: **30 days** for month‑to‑month leases, or the notice period specified in the lease.
• Landlords must provide a written notice of termination. | • Keep copies of all notices. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlords must follow the Texas **eviction procedure**: serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice to pay rent or quit), file a lawsuit, and obtain a court order.
• You have the right to contest the eviction in court. | • Respond promptly to notices.
• Seek legal aid if you’re facing eviction. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major defect after notice, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from your rent, but only after giving the landlord a written notice and a reasonable deadline. | • Keep receipts and document the defect. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live in the unit without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • Report any disturbances (e.g., excessive noise, trespassing). | | **Subletting** | • The lease may restrict subletting, but if it does, the landlord cannot unreasonably deny a sublet request. | • Ask for written permission if you plan to sublet. | | **Insurance** | • Landlords are not required to provide insurance for your personal property, but you can obtain renter’s insurance to protect your belongings. | • Consider renter’s insurance for peace of mind. | ### Quick Resources | Resource | What It Offers | How to Access | |----------|----------------|---------------| | **Texas Attorney General – Tenant Rights** | Detailed guide on tenant rights and responsibilities. | https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights** | File discrimination complaints. | https://www.tchra.texas.gov | | **Legal Aid of North Texas** | Free legal help for low‑income tenants. | https://www.legalaidnt.org | | **Texas Eviction Hotline** | 1‑800‑555‑1234 (example number; check local hotlines). | Call or visit website. | --- #### Bottom Line - **Document everything** (photos, receipts, written notices). - **Know your lease** and the specific terms it contains. - **Act promptly** when issues arise—report problems in writing and give the landlord a reasonable deadline to fix them. - **Seek help** if you believe your rights are being violated—contact a local tenant‑rights group, legal aid, or the appropriate state agency. If you have a specific situation (e.g., a dispute over a security deposit, a repair that hasn’t been fixed, or a potential eviction notice), let me know and I can give more tailored guidance.
